To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

purslane (Portula oleracea L.), a wild vegetable crop, is a rich source of bioactive compounds, which are augmented in the presence of salinity, and thus can be harnosed for possible human health and economical benefits.
the purslane accessions Ac5, Ac4, Ac6, Ac7 and Ac8 possessed potential for salinity-induced production of bioactive compound which in turn can serve for possible human health benefit.

salinity-induced augmented levels of bioactive compounds in some purslane accessions which in turn can have possible human health benefits and can also be harnessed as a source of natural antioxidant.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the possible use of purslane as a salinity-tolerant crop for bioactive compounds production and its potential for human health benefits.
the potential of purslane for economical use.
the possible economical use of purslane for the production of bioactive compound in response to salinity stress.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the salinity-induced augmented levels of bioactive compounds in some of these purslane accessions can be harnosed for possible economical use.
the salinity-induced augmented contents of bioactive compounds in selected purslane accessions could be a potential source of natural antioxidants for possible human health and economical use.
salinity treatment resulted into significant increase in the contents of total phenolics, total flavonoids and antioxidant activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
purslane is a potential plant species with a high level of tolerance to salt stress and is a potential source of bioactive compounds for possible human health applications.
salinity-induced augmented levels of total phenolics and flavonoids and antioxidant activity in purslane could be harnessed as a potential economical crop.
salinity-induced augmented TPC, TFC and FRAP activity of purslane accessions Ac6, Ac8, Ac4, and Ac5 could be harnessed to produce a novel food supplement.
The main takeaway from our work is that
purslane is a promising plant for the development of functional food and nutraceuticals.
salinity-induced augmented levels of bioactive compounds in some purslane accessions can be used for economical purposes.
purslane accessions with high TPC and TCC could be used as a potential source of antioxidants and bioactive compounds for the development of functional foods, nutraceuticals and pharmaceuticals.
